title: Welcome to ZEHN
text: ZEHN means 'mind' in Urdu, and this campus is built to study it. Each building around the courtyard holds one part of psychology, from neurons to neighbourhoods. Over sixteen weeks you will learn, experience, design, run, analyse and report your own research.

title: Wundt Hall
text: This hall is named after Wilhelm Wundt, who set up one of the first laboratories devoted to experimental psychology in Leipzig. His students trained across Europe and North America and spread the idea that the mind could be studied with controlled methods. The timeline inside traces how that idea grew.

title: Schools and Perspectives
text: Structuralism, functionalism, psychoanalysis, behaviourism, humanism and cognitivism each asked different questions about the mind. Modern psychology keeps several lenses at once: biological, cognitive, behavioural, developmental and sociocultural. The Perspectives Lens lets you explain one behaviour through each of them.

title: The Methods Library
text: Every claim in psychology rests on a research design. Experiments manipulate a variable and use random assignment to support causal conclusions; correlational and observational studies describe relationships without that control. The Research Methods Lab lets you build each design and see what it can and cannot tell you.

title: The IRB Chamber
text: Before any study runs, an ethics board checks that risks are minimised, consent is informed and participants can withdraw without penalty. Modern review grew out of historical abuses and principles such as respect for persons, beneficence and justice. Here you will judge proposals and learn why a board says approve, revise or reject.

title: Data Sculptures
text: The histograms around you are built from the class dataset. Mean, median and mode describe the centre of a distribution, while the standard deviation describes its spread. Watch how one extreme value pulls the mean but barely moves the median.

title: Correlation Is Not Causation
text: A correlation coefficient runs from -1 to +1 and describes the direction and strength of a linear relationship. Two variables can move together because a third variable drives both. Drag points on the scatterplot to see how a single outlier changes r.

title: The Neuro Atrium
text: Neurons communicate with electrical signals inside the cell and chemical signals between cells. Dendrites receive input, the axon carries output, and glial cells support and insulate the network. The bridge ahead is a giant model neuron you can walk along.

title: The Synapse Chamber
text: When an action potential reaches the axon terminal, neurotransmitter is released into the synaptic cleft. It binds to receptors on the next cell and can make that cell more or less likely to fire. Reuptake and enzymes then clear the cleft, which is where many medications act.

title: Walk-Through Brain
text: Fly from the brainstem, which supports basic life functions, up through the limbic structures to the cerebral cortex. The cortex is divided into frontal, parietal, temporal and occipital lobes, each linked to different functions. The split-brain table shows what happens when the two hemispheres can no longer share information directly.

title: The Sleep Lab
text: Sleep is an active state with repeating cycles of non-REM and REM stages. Researchers track these stages with EEG, eye-movement and muscle recordings. Watch the simulated overnight record and notice how the cycles change across the night.

title: The Staircase Booth
text: Psychophysics links physical stimulus intensity to what we experience. A staircase procedure moves the stimulus up after a miss and down after a hit until it settles near your threshold. Weber's law says the just-noticeable difference grows in proportion to the starting intensity.

title: Rooms That Lie
text: The Ames room looks rectangular from one viewpoint but is actually distorted, so people inside seem to change size. Illusions such as Müller-Lyer and Ponzo show that perception is an active interpretation of cues, not a copy of the world. Measure each illusion yourself with the method of adjustment.

title: Attention Cubicles
text: Attention selects some information and filters out the rest. In visual search, a target defined by a single feature can seem to pop out, while a target defined by a combination of features usually takes longer to find. The Stroop task shows how hard it is to ignore a word you can read.

title: The Plaza Event
text: When attention is busy with a demanding task, people can fail to notice an unexpected object in plain view. This is called inattentional blindness. After the plaza event you will receive a full debrief explaining what was hidden and why.

title: The Pavlov Station
text: In classical conditioning, a neutral stimulus paired with a meaningful one comes to trigger a response on its own. The Rescorla–Wagner model describes learning as driven by prediction error: the gap between what happens and what was expected. Run acquisition, extinction and spontaneous recovery to watch the curve change.

title: Skinner Boxes
text: Operant conditioning changes behaviour through its consequences. Fixed and variable schedules of reinforcement produce different response patterns, which a cumulative recorder draws as a rising line. Shaping builds new behaviour by reinforcing closer and closer approximations.

title: The Memory Palace
text: The method of loci links items to places along a familiar route, then retrieves them by walking the route in imagination. It works by combining vivid imagery with an organised retrieval structure. Build your own palace here and test it against plain rote rehearsal.

title: The Eyewitness Street
text: Memory is reconstructive, so later information can change what people report. Leading questions and misleading details can alter eyewitness accounts. Research like this has shaped recommendations for fairer interviews and line-ups.

title: The Mental-Rotation Bench
text: Decide whether two 3D shapes are the same object turned around or mirror images. In classic studies, response time tends to rise as the angle between the shapes increases, as if the shape were being turned in the mind. Your own data will show whether you follow that pattern.

title: Problems and Tests
text: The Tower of Hanoi shows planning with sub-goals, and the Wason selection task shows how people often look for confirming evidence. Intelligence tests try to measure reasoning abilities, but every test reflects choices about content, culture and norms. ZEHN uses only original puzzles, never protected test items.

title: Behind the One-Way Mirror
text: Developmental researchers often observe rather than question young children. Reliable observation needs clear behaviour codes and a check that two coders agree. All children here are simulated characters.

title: Conservation and Theory of Mind
text: Piaget proposed that children come to understand that quantity stays the same when only its appearance changes. False-belief tasks ask whether a child understands that someone else can hold a belief that is wrong. Later research shows that task wording and culture can change when children succeed.

title: The FACS Face Lab
text: The Facial Action Coding System describes expressions as combinations of muscle movements called action units. Move the sliders to build a face one action unit at a time. Whether expressions are read the same way across cultures is still debated.

title: Stress and Health
text: When a situation is appraised as threatening, the HPA axis and the sympathetic nervous system prepare the body to respond. Short-term activation can help, but long-lasting stress is linked to poorer health. Coping, social support and sleep all shape how stress affects us.

title: The Test-Construction Studio
text: Trait models describe personality along broad dimensions such as the Big Five. ZEHN uses public-domain IPIP items, and your results are for learning only, not a diagnosis. Compare your profile with the simulated class distribution.

title: Reliability and Validity
text: A reliable test gives consistent results; a valid test measures what it claims to measure. Cronbach's alpha estimates internal consistency from how well items agree with each other. A test can be reliable without being valid, but not the other way round.

title: The Mohalla
text: The crowd in this street follows simple social-psychology rules for conformity, helping and cooperation. Change one rule and watch group behaviour shift. Every agent is simulated; no real person is portrayed.

title: The Asch Room
text: In Asch-style studies, a participant hears a group give a clearly wrong answer before giving their own. The study involves deception, so you will receive a full debrief and the option to delete your data. I-O psychology applies the same group processes to teams and workplaces.

title: The Counselling Centre
text: Psychological disorders are described by patterns of distress and impaired functioning, not by single symptoms. Every client here is simulated, and ZEHN never screens or labels you. For official criteria, see DSM-5-TR or ICD-11.

title: The First Session
text: A first session covers consent, confidentiality and its limits before any problem is explored. Skills such as open questions, affirmations, reflections and summaries help clients feel heard. Culture shapes how people describe distress and what help they seek.

title: Replication and Open Science
text: Large replication projects have found that some published effects are smaller than first reported or do not repeat. Preregistration, open data and larger samples help make findings more trustworthy. Every replication you run here reports an honest outcome.

title: The Poster Hall
text: Science is not finished until it is communicated. Turn your analysis into an APA-style results paragraph and a poster. Then defend it, including the limitations.

title: Graduation in the Courtyard
text: You have walked from the history of psychology to running your own replications. Every building you visited holds a lab you can return to and a mission you can extend. Elective tracks in clinical, cognitive neuroscience, developmental, educational, forensic, health and I-O psychology are now open.
